transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what finally brought me in is... I just feel like a part of me has gone very quiet. The part that used to reach out to people, or take pleasure in things. I'm a social worker, and I used to really care about my work. I enjoyed yoga, going to galleries, even just journaling. But lately, I don't feel much of anything toward them. I'm mostly just... moving through my obligations.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life, or is this the first time you have felt this way?

No, I don't think I have. This is really the first time I've felt this way. I mean, I've had times where I was tired or maybe a little burned out from work—that's pretty normal in my field—but it never felt like this. This kind of... emptiness, I guess, is completely new for me.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been about eight months. I'd say this whole change in how I'm thinking and working, and just connecting with people... it really started around the time we took my older relative into our apartment. So, yeah, it's been going on since then.

Looking back over your entire life, even going back to your teenage years or early adulthood, can you recall any other periods lasting at least two weeks where you felt this same persistent emptiness or loss of interest?

No, I really can't. Like I said, I've had normal stress and burnout from work, but never anything like this. I've never had a period where I felt this empty or lost interest in things for two weeks or more. This is definitely the first time.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep patterns since you started feeling this way?
No, not really. My sleep has been pretty much the same. I still go to bed around the same time and wake up when my alarm goes off. I haven't noticed any real changes there.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight since this started eight months ago?
No, my appetite has been pretty normal. I'm eating about the same amount I usually do, and my weight hasn't really changed at all. So, no, nothing different there.
Aside from the loss of interest, have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking in energy throughout the day?

No, I haven't really noticed that. My energy levels are... well, they're pretty much the same as always. I mean, I get tired at the end of the day just from work, but it's not an unusual lack of energy or anything. I still have enough energy to get through my normal routine.
Do you find yourself feeling excessively guilty about things, or do you feel like you are worthless?

No, I don't have feelings like that. I don't feel guilty about anything in particular, and I certainly don't feel worthless. I mean, I know I'm capable and I do my job well, so... no, I haven't been struggling with those kinds of thoughts at all.
Aside from the loss of interest you've described, have you been feeling sad, down, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day?

No, not really. I mean, I don't feel sad or down. I definitely don't feel hopeless. My mood is just... normal, I guess. I just don't have the interest in things like I used to, but it's not because I'm depressed or crying all the time. I just feel fine, mood-wise.
Do you feel that the way you are reacting to having your relative live with you is more intense or overwhelming than what one would typically expect for that kind of situation?

No, I don't think so. I mean... having a relative move in is always an adjustment, but I wouldn't say my reaction is more intense or overwhelming than normal. It's just standard stress, really. I think most people would react pretty much the exact same way I am.
Even though you feel you are coping, has this shift in your interest and engagement caused any significant problems or distress in your daily life or your relationships?

Well, I mean, it has definitely affected things at work. I'm still showing up every day, but... I'm just not functioning at my usual level. I've actually missed a few important grant deadlines recently, which isn't like me. And my supervisor, she hasn't made a big deal out of it, but I've noticed she's quietly moved some of my more demanding clients over to other clinicians. So, yeah, it is causing some problems there, even if I'm still going through the motions.
Do you feel that your loss of interest and the resulting decline in your work performance would improve if your relative were no longer living with you?

I don't think so. I mean, my relative moving in is an adjustment, sure, but... I really don't feel like that's the reason I've lost interest in my work. Even if they moved out tomorrow, I think I'd still be struggling to care about the grants or my clients. The two things just don't feel connected to me.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating on your tasks or making decisions lately?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with that. I mean... I can still focus on what I'm doing when I need to, and making decisions hasn't been a problem. It's more just... not having the drive to do it, rather than not being able to concentrate.
Beyond the loss of interest in your hobbies and work, do you feel a general sense of emotional detachment or numbness in your day-to-day life, as if you are observing yourself from the outside?

No, I wouldn't say I feel numb or detached like that. I don't feel like I'm watching myself from the outside. I'm still present... I feel my emotions normally, I think. It's really just the lack of interest and motivation that's the issue, not feeling disconnected from myself.
